info.title: MaintenancePizza API
info.description:
Ticket system microservice for store maintenance. An authenticated user files a ticket describing the issues in a store; dispatchers then drive each issue through its lifecycle (diagnosis, technician assignment, attendance, parts, pay/driving, warranty) until completion.

Key design notes:
- All endpoints require a Sanctum bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). There are no login/registration endpoints in this service — tokens are issued elsewhere.
- Most endpoints are store-scoped under `/api/stores/{store}`, where `{store}` is the store NUMBER (e.g. `03795-00001`), not a numeric id.
- The system is append-only apart from one exception: `PATCH .../issues/{ticketIssue}` re-points an issue at a different catalog issue. Everything else is corrected by marking leaf records `mistaken` and creating new ones; lifecycle changes are explicit POST actions.
- A ticket's status is DERIVED from its issues and is never set directly.
- Workflow records (diagnosis, attendance, parts, pay, warranty, assignment, technicians) attach to ONE OR MANY issues via `ticket_issue_ids`, enabling flexible grouping.
- Every entity (tickets, issues, workflow records, catalog items, stores) accepts any number of polymorphic Notes and Attachments via dedicated POST endpoints.
- Notes are stored with their author (`created_by`), optional `type`, and may carry their own file attachments.
- Ticket closing notes are typed with FinalNoteType (`final_notes` or `what_we_learned`) and are appended via the `/final-note` endpoint.
- Issues (and tickets by derivation) now support a `cancelled` status in addition to the existing statuses.

tags.name: Storage
tags.description: Parts inventory across one or more storage locations. Stock is an append-only ledger of movements: on-hand is SUM(quantity × direction) over every movement line, and a mistake is corrected by recording an equal-and-opposite reversal rather than by editing. Taking a part out of storage on a ticket writes a movement automatically.

tags.name: Daily Pay
tags.description:
End-of-day payment records, in three levels: an entry is one date, it holds one payment per payee, and each payment holds one line per store. A payee is a Technician row — a company is simply a technician named after the company — so a single payment can cover several stores at once.

Each payment gathers its own figures from records that already exist: the hours clocked against its issues, and the parts somebody other than us paid for. Those are FROZEN when the entry is saved, so a signed-off pay sheet does not change when a ticket is corrected later; POST .../recalculate re-pulls them on demand.

Editing replaces the payments wholesale while keeping a JSON snapshot of the prior state as revision history.

get.description:
`summary`: KPIs, tickets filed in the range (each issue flagged when it recurs at that store), and chart series (by issue, by store, open work by status, completions by issue with average hours).

`activity`: the tickets that changed in the range (the ticket or one of its issues has updated_at in it), most recently changed first, paginated -- each with `changes`: whether it was opened then, its issues' status changes (title, from, to, by, at), and how many notes and files were added. Locked notes are never counted.

`watchlist`: now -- open tickets with no change for `untouched_days` (default 1) or more, longest silence first (`last_change_at`, `days_silent`); and catalog issues reported on at least `recurring_min` tickets at one store in the `recurring_days` days up to `to`.

`from`/`to` are INSTANTS: send the viewer's local midnights converted to UTC, so 'yesterday' is the viewer's yesterday.

`finances` (docs/MAINTENANCE.md §6): where the money went. `from`/`to` are DATES (YYYY-MM-DD; an instant is cut to its date), both included, at most 400 days. Summed from payment LINES; mistaken payments excluded. Filters (AND): `stores[]` = lines at those stores (other-store and storage lines drop out), `category_id` = lines of payments to technicians of that category (supplier payments drop out), `technician_id`, `supplier_id`. `totals.previous_spent` is the same number of days immediately before; `change_pct` is null when that was 0. `trend` is per ISO week (`period` = the Monday, YYYY-MM-DD) up to 92 days, per month (YYYY-MM) beyond, every period present. `by_store[].store_number` is a store number, `other` (other-store lines) or `storage` (parts bought for the shelf). `by_category` is technician categories only (id null = no category). A line linked to several ticket issues is shared evenly between them in `tickets.*`. `estimate_vs_actual` uses each issue's latest non-mistaken inspection estimate vs. what was paid on it in the range (top 50 by actual). `approvals_by_level` counts APPROVED, non-mistaken approvals decided in the range (store filter only), in the settings' level order. `recurring_costly`: the same catalog issue at the same store on 2+ tickets with spend in the range. `stock` ignores the payment filters (storage is global): `on_hand_value` = positive balances now x average cost; the others are the range's Bought / Used / Stock count (-/+) / Damaged or lost lines, each at its own unit cost, else the part's average cost (quantity-weighted cost of every priced inbound line; mistaken and undone movements left out). `unpaid` is what is owed NOW (not limited to the range): closed, non-mistaken sessions with no claim by a non-mistaken payment, and unpaid, non-mistaken technician purchases; filtered by technician/category (a supplier filter gives zeros), and by stores via the trip's stops / the purchase's ticket or stop.

`coverage`: `stores[]` (default: every store that has had a ticket), `issue_ids[]` (default: every catalog issue not deleted), `category_id`. A technician (not deleted) covers a cell when he covers the store (coverage_stores) and the issue (covered issues). One cell per store x issue, ordered by store number then issue title. `gap` = technicians <= 1; `gaps` counts them. `average_rating` is the average of the non-null per-issue ratings of the cell's technicians (1-decimal string). KPIs: distinct technicians covering at least one requested store / issue / both; `emergency_available` = of those covering both, the ones available for emergencies.

`stores[]` is required (at least one) for summary, activity and watchlist only.

updated_at.description: Last change to the ticket or anything on it: its issues, their records, notes and files touch it.

analytics.description: Present only when include_analytics=true was passed

total.description: Issues matching the active filters (i.e. 'new' issues when scoped via a date filter)

status_breakdown.description: All 7 IssueStatus values always present, zero-filled when absent. status_breakdown[status=complete].count is 'how many completed'.

durations.description: Averages in seconds/hours; null with sample_size 0 when no issue matches

avg_tickets_per_week.description: Always all-time (ignores created_from/to and changed_from/to; still respects every other active filter). Custom week runs Tuesday 00:00:00 through Monday 23:59:59.

weeks_spanned.description: Weeks between the earliest and latest matching ticket, inclusive; weeks with zero tickets still count

TicketType.description: Ticket type: normal issue or preventive maintenance.

type.description: Ticket type. Defaults to 'normal' when omitted.

issues.description: One or more issue lines. Each line uses either a catalog issue_id OR a free-text other_title.

issue_id.description: Catalog issue id. Provide this OR other_title, not both.

other_title.description: Free-text issue title. Required when issue_id is absent.

notes.description: Optional notes to attach to this issue at creation time (text only; use POST …/notes to add files to notes afterward).

troubleshooting_version.description: The version of that guide shown. A mismatch (the guide changed) is a 422.

troubleshooting.description: How troubleshooting went. Required for an issue that has guides with steps.

troubleshooting_guide_id.description: Optional: the guide that matched the problem. Must be one of the issue's guides.

issues.*.files[].description: Files to attach directly to this issue (multipart only — field name issues[N][files][]).

notes.description: Optional notes to attach to the ticket itself at creation time.

files[].description: Files to attach directly to the ticket (requires multipart/form-data).

CreateOtherTicketRequest.description: Request body for POST /tickets (the 'Others' flow). Supply other_store instead of a store in the URL.

other_store.description: Free-text description of the location or store not present in the system.

type.description: Ticket type. Defaults to 'normal' when omitted.

issues.description: One or more issue lines. Each line uses either a catalog issue_id OR a free-text other_title.

issue_id.description: Catalog issue id. Provide this OR other_title, not both.

other_title.description: Free-text issue title. Required when issue_id is absent.

troubleshooting_version.description: The version of that guide shown. A mismatch (the guide changed) is a 422.

troubleshooting.description: How troubleshooting went. Required for an issue that has guides with steps.

troubleshooting_guide_id.description: Optional: the guide that matched the problem. Must be one of the issue's guides.

notes.description: Optional notes to attach to the ticket itself at creation time.

files[].description: Files to attach directly to the ticket (requires multipart/form-data).

IssueHistoryRow.description: One earlier ticket at the store that reported the same catalog issue. `issues` holds that ticket's rows for the issue (a deferral chain, or the same issue reported twice); `status` is where the newest of them stands.

TroubleshootingGuide.description: What to try for one specific problem with a catalog issue. An issue can have several.

steps.description: In order: what to try first, then next. Each step carries its own files.

version.description: Goes up on every save. Send it back when opening a ticket after trying this guide.

fixed_count.description: Times stores said this guide fixed the problem (no ticket opened).

not_fixed_count.description: Tickets opened after trying this guide.

TechnicianAbility.description: How good a technician is at one catalog issue.

call_first.description: The one to call first for this issue. At most one technician per issue.

TechnicianOverallRating.description: A technician's overall rating. Same shape as TechnicianAbility without the issue.

call_first.description: The one to call first for anything. At most one technician overall.

steps.description: Blank rows are dropped; at least one real step. A step sent with its id is kept, with its files; steps left out are removed.
